alyssa: Heads-up: I want to split the dedicated-pool autoscaler into two coordinated pieces: a tiny synchronous micro-admit on the runtime hot path and an async planner/controller that issues timeboxed leases and drives prewarms. Rationale: keep latency-critical admits O(1) while letting the controller optimize cost.
kevin: Curious how you avoid conflicts. If micro-admit grants slots that planner didn't expect, could we overcommit capacity?
alyssa: Micro-admit is conservative: it only uses a small local budget (burst slots + headroom window) and observes a summarized lease footprint emitted by the controller. If controller later can't materialize capacity, it revokes via TTL expiry and increments a churn metric.
sam: How do we detect oscillation and prevent thrash between micro-admit and planner?
alyssa: Use three mechanisms: (1) planner issues leases with TTL and version ids; (2) micro-admit respects a soft headroom counter that decays slowly; (3) controller adapts aggressiveness if churn > threshold (automatic damping).
jordan: Operator API changes? we should avoid big breaking CRD edits.
alyssa: Minimal additive change: optional `scaling_profiles` array. Default is legacy mode. Example snippet: ```scaling_profiles:
- name: fastpath
  micro_admit:
    burst_slots: 3
    headroom_ms: 200
  planner:
    horizon_s: 60
    cost_bias: 0.6
    reserve_ttl_s: 300
```
marie: Metrics to track: micro-admit hit rate, planner-reserved vs actual provisioned, churn rate (revokes/TTL), p99 admit latency, cost/token. Also add an alert if revokes/sec spikes.
kevin: Can orch-bot run a simulated trace w/ last 10d of pool alpha and compare legacy vs split-regime?
orch-bot: queued sim `sim-8342223333-legacy-vs-split` for pool alpha using 10d trace. ETA 16m. Will post admission timelines and churn heatmap. :robot_face:
sam: After sim, I'll run a 6h canary on alpha (10% traffic) with the split regime and the conservative profile. I'll own dashboards.
jordan: Runtime hook request: `is_micro_admit_ok(profile_version)` that must be allocation-free and return quickly. Keep caller code minimal.
alyssa: Agreed. Micro-admit must be inlined in runtime and only consult an atomic counter snapshot + the summarized lease footprint. Controller emits footprint via operator CRD status.
marie: I'll author a short runbook: automatic stabilization actions (widen headroom, increase TTL) if churn> X for 5m, and an incident page for repeated revokes.
alyssa: I'll draft the RFC with CRD diff and a short compatibility note. Will link sim results when orch-bot posts.
